name: frontend
description: Family Greenhouse web app — React + TypeScript + Vite PWA for collaborative household plant care.

scripts.build: tsc -b && vite build && vite build --ssr src/entry-server.tsx --outDir dist-ssr && node scripts/prerender.mjs

_size-limit-note: Budgets are REGRESSION GATES set ~8% above the current measured size (brotli), not aspirational targets — the old values (40/60/230/10) were below what the app has ever shipped, so the check was permanently red and gated nothing. Trimming the bundle further (the index chunk and Tailwind CSS are the candidates) is tracked as future work for when real-device Lighthouse data shows it matters. Keep these tight: lower them whenever a real reduction lands. Measured with @size-limit/file (brotli) only — the preset-app 'time' plugin ran headless Chrome to estimate JS execution time, gated nothing (no time budgets), and broke CI+local runs with puppeteer navigation timeouts. Vendor budget raised 51 → 64 kB for the React 18 → 19 upgrade: react-dom 19 is ~12 kB (brotli) larger than 18, putting the React runtime chunk at ~59.5 kB measured — a sanctioned, unavoidable dependency increase, not regression drift; 64 kB keeps the usual ~8% headroom. All-JS-combined budget raised 312 → 320 kB when the care-guide content surface grew (six new species pages + two blog posts): the prose lands in the lazy careGuides/BlogPost chunks, so the Initial JS and Vendor budgets are untouched — only the combined aggregate moved, to ~312.4 kB measured. This is sanctioned content growth, not regression drift; 320 kB keeps a tight ~2.5% cushion. All-JS-combined budget raised 320 → 330 kB for the v0.8.0 feature backlog (annual + lifetime billing UI, the no-care-data notice, server-confirmed analytics): the additions land in the lazy billing/settings and feature chunks, so the Initial JS (~60.4 kB) and Vendor budgets keep healthy headroom and only the aggregate moved, to ~320.1 kB measured — sanctioned growth, not regression drift; 330 kB restores a tight ~3% cushion. The v0.15.0 name nursery plus the already-merged React Router 7 runtime moved the measured aggregate to 331 kB while keeping initial JS at 47.3 kB; 340 kB restores a tight 2.7% regression cushion. All-JS-combined raised 340 → 348 kB for the Capacitor mobile shells: the @capacitor/core + push-notifications runtime lands in a lazy chunk that is dynamically imported ONLY inside the iOS/Android apps (web platform detection reads the injected window.Capacitor global precisely so web visitors never fetch it — see src/lib/platform.ts), moving the aggregate to ~337.7 kB measured while Initial JS (48.7 kB) and Vendor budgets are untouched; 348 kB keeps a tight ~3% cushion.
_size-limit-note-0-17: All-JS-combined raised 348 → 360 kB for the location-aware plant move workflow: the 349.39 kB measured aggregate includes the new 2.71 kB-gzip MovePlantsDialog lazy chunk, while Initial JS (11.88 kB), Vendor (61.32 kB), and CSS (14.59 kB) remain within their existing budgets. The 360 kB limit restores a tight ~3% regression cushion without relaxing any critical-path budget.
_size-limit-note-0-21: All-JS-combined raised 360 → 374 kB when free-account registration reopened: the 362.74 kB measured aggregate includes the restored lazy signup flow, confirmation recovery, and localized public acquisition copy. Initial JS (13.61 kB), Vendor (61.26 kB), and CSS (10.04 kB) remain within their existing budgets; only the aggregate moved. The 374 kB limit restores a tight ~3% regression cushion without relaxing a critical-path budget.
_size-limit-note-0-23: All-JS-combined raised 374 -> 386 kB for the paid-plan purchase surface: the 374.56 kB measured aggregate includes the new PaidPlanGrid, its interval toggle, the checkout and billing-portal controls, and ~60 new i18n keys across en + es. Every one of those lands in the lazy pricing/settings chunks, so the critical-path budgets are untouched and still hold wide margins - Initial JS 14.6 kB (limit 62), Vendor 59.85 kB (limit 64), CSS 12.54 kB (limit 15). Only the aggregate moved, and by 556 B. Sanctioned feature growth, not regression drift; 386 kB restores a tight ~3% cushion without relaxing any critical-path budget.
_size-limit-note-blog-expansion: All-JS-combined raised 386 -> 402 kB for the blog content expansion (eight new posts: shared-household care, travel/plant-sitter handover, and the overwatering / yellow-leaves / room-light diagnostics). Every word lands in the lazy `posts` chunk that only /blog/:slug pulls, so no critical-path budget moved: Initial JS 14.6 kB (limit 62), Vendor 59.85 kB (limit 64), CSS 12.5 kB (limit 15) are all unchanged. Only the aggregate moved, to 389.69 kB measured. Sanctioned content growth, not regression drift; 402 kB restores the usual ~3% cushion without relaxing a critical-path budget.
_size-limit-note-help-content: All-JS-combined raised 402 -> 435 kB, sized once for the two content surfaces landing together: the nine public /help/:topicId pages (this branch, #389) and the 14 species care guides (#384). Measured on a post-#391 build, which is the only build that counts here - prerendering changed the emitted output and moved the main baseline 389.69 -> 394.57 kB, so every earlier reading is stale. Against that baseline: help alone 405.22 kB (+10.65), care guides alone 411.6 kB (+17.03), both together 422.25 kB (+27.68) measured. 435 kB is 3.0% over the combined figure, the usual cushion, and both branches carry the same value so it is merge-order independent. This supersedes an earlier note on this branch claiming a 386 -> 397 kB raise: main never sat at 397, the branch inherited 402 from #383, and 397 would not have held the measured size in any case. The growth is the help answers themselves - helpContent is a 61.95 kB raw chunk that only /help and /help/:topicId pull, and App.tsx already lazy-loads both routes. Lazy-loading bounds what a visitor downloads, not this budget: `dist/assets/*.js` globs all 97 emitted chunks, so splitting cannot move this number, which is why #383 raised the limit for the blog posts while correctly calling them lazy. Nine public help pages earn it: they are the pages that answer 'how do I cancel' and 'I cannot log in' for signed-out users, they are prerendered to real HTML for search, and each answer carries a plain-text twin that feeds the FAQPage JSON-LD. No critical-path budget moved: Initial JS 15.63 kB (limit 62), Vendor 59.93 kB (limit 64), CSS 12.6 kB (limit 15), against 15.6 / 59.98 / 12.52 on main - flat to within 80 B, and not one of those three limits is relaxed. Sanctioned content growth, not regression drift.
_size-limit-note-0-23-legal-i18n: Legal-page i18n move: no budget change, but the cushion is now thin. The privacy, terms, support and account-deletion prose moved into the i18n catalogs (101 keys x 2 locales), growing the startup i18n chunk 122.07 -> 158.91 kB raw (33.80 -> 43.97 kB brotli) and the measured All-JS-combined aggregate 423.05 -> 433.15 kB brotli (+10.10). Re-measured against main after #389 (public help pages), #390 (payments-live legal corrections) and #384 (14 care guides) had all landed; the earlier reading on this branch (375.91 -> 386.26 kB, proposing a 386 -> 398 kB raise) predates all three and is stale, and the 402 -> 435 hunk it carried is now a no-op because main already sits at 435. This branch therefore raises nothing and relaxes nothing: 435 kB, set by #389 and #384 for the help and care-guide content surfaces, still holds. It holds by 1.85 kB - a 0.43% cushion, not the ~3% this file usually keeps - because 435 was sized for those two content surfaces and did not budget for this catalog growth on top. Read that as a real signal, not a rounding error: the next content or catalog addition will breach it, and the fix is the deferred work below rather than another raise. No critical-path budget moved: Initial JS 15.63 kB (limit 62, against 15.66 on main), Vendor 59.93 kB (limit 64, unchanged), CSS 12.6 kB (limit 15, unchanged). Unlike the lazy pricing/help/care chunks, both catalogs load at startup by design, so this 10 kB lands on every visit even though Spanish is still gated off; the follow-up is a lazily-added `legal` namespace (i18n.addResourceBundle from the legal routes) that would return it to the startup path and restore the cushion without touching the limit.
_size-limit-note-0-23-calendar-feed: All-JS-combined raised 435 -> 450 kB for the revocable calendar-feed link, and to clear an overage main was already carrying. Both readings were taken in one worktree with one npm ci, same tree and same node_modules, on this branch rebased onto main at 5d3c5be. Main alone measures 435.89 kB and is ALREADY 893 B over the 435 kB limit: the gate went red on main itself when #394 (onboarding activation) landed, and CI's own Bundle size run on adf2e53 reports that identical 435.89 kB / 893 B pair, so this is main's drift reproduced, not a local artifact. This branch measures 437.53 kB, so its own contribution is 1.64 kB and it is exactly where this feature should land: +944 B in the startup i18n chunk (27 new keys x en + es) and +667 B in the lazy AccountSettings chunk (the mint / reveal-once / revoke / regenerate UI plus calendarFeedService). Every other chunk moves by tens of bytes of hashing noise and no new chunk is emitted. No critical-path budget moved - Initial JS 15.66 kB (limit 62), Vendor 59.94 kB (limit 64) and CSS 12.6 kB (limit 15) are byte-identical on main and on this branch. 450 kB is 2.9% over the measured 437.53 kB, restoring the ~3% cushion that the note above recorded falling to 0.43%. Most of what this raise buys back is main's, not this branch's: the deferred lazy `legal` namespace described in that note is still the real fix for the startup i18n chunk, and it is now overdue - the next content or catalog addition should land it rather than take another raise.
_size-limit-note-0-23-deferred-legal-cat: Deferred legal catalog: NO budget change, and a measurement that closes out the follow-up the two notes above kept deferring. `_size-limit-note-0-23-legal-i18n` named the fix (a lazily-added `legal` namespace via i18n.addResourceBundle from the legal routes) and `_size-limit-note-0-23-calendar-feed` called it overdue. This is that fix. THE MOVE: the 101 privacy/terms/support/account-deletion keys per locale left `locales/<lng>/translation.json` for `locales/<lng>/legal.json`, which src/i18n/legalCatalog.ts merges into the `translation` namespace with addResourceBundle, on demand, from the four legal routes only. App.tsx awaits that load inside each route's React.lazy() factory, in parallel with the page chunk, so the copy is registered before the component mounts - on navigation, on hydration of a prerendered page, and in the build-time prerender, whose react-dom/static prerender() waits on the same promise. /legal/privacy and /legal/terms come out of the prerender byte-identical to main, asset hashes aside (8,513 and 4,301 characters of prose, zero raw keys). Keys are unchanged and still `legal.*`-rooted, so no call site moved, and check-i18n-catalogs.mjs gates both files (NAMESPACES is now ['translation','legal']): 875 en / 894 es keys before and after, none dropped. WHAT IT BOUGHT, AND WHERE: the startup i18n chunk fell 175.93 -> 139.10 kB raw and 48.30 -> 38.20 kB brotli. Every visit now ships 36.83 kB raw / 10.11 kB brotli less, in both locales, including a build where Spanish is still gated off; net of the loader and lazy wrapper (+138 B on Initial JS) that is 9.97 kB brotli off the startup path for every visitor. WHAT IT DID NOT BUY, MEASURED: the All-JS-combined aggregate did not fall. It rose, 444.06 -> 444.88 kB (+827 B). `All-JS-combined` globs dist/assets/*.js - all 99 emitted chunks - and @size-limit/file brotli-compresses each file separately and sums them, so the same prose costs MORE once it has its own chunk (10.83 kB standalone) than it did interleaved in a large shared one (10.11 kB in-context). `_size-limit-note-help-content` already said splitting cannot lower this number; this is the measurement showing it raises it slightly, and it corrects the expectation in the two notes above that a deferred namespace would restore this budget's cushion. It cannot, and no further split of this catalog will: this budget counts bytes emitted, not bytes downloaded, so the win is real but lands somewhere this gate does not look. Read that as a property of the gate, not a reason to skip the fix - and as a limit on what this budget is for. It is a good regression gate on total emitted JS and a blind one on delivery: any work that moves bytes off the startup path without deleting them (deferred namespaces, route-scoped catalogs, on-demand chunks) will look flat or slightly negative here while being a real win for users. Judge that class of change on the startup-chunk figures recorded above, not on this number, and do not let a flat aggregate argue against doing it. NO LIMIT MOVES: 450 kB, set by #399, still holds - 444.88 kB measured leaves a 1.14% cushion where main already sat at 1.34%, so this branch spends 827 B of an existing cushion and neither raises nor lowers anything. Lowering the limit was considered and is not supported by the measurement. No critical-path budget moves either - Initial JS 15.83 kB (limit 62, against 15.69 on main), Vendor 60.01 kB (limit 64, unchanged), CSS 12.66 kB (limit 15, unchanged). Measured with `npm ci && cd frontend && npm run build && npm run size`, main and branch back to back in one worktree on one node_modules, Node 26.8.1 / npm 11.19.0; main reads 444.06 kB here, the same figure #420 reported, so this pair is reproducible across environments rather than a local artifact. ONE INTERACTION TO WATCH: PR #419 (not on main as of 55832fa) pins `src/i18n/locales/` to a named `i18n` chunk in vite.config.ts. As written that rule also captures locales/<lng>/legal.json and folds the prose back into a modulepreloaded chunk - measured, the deferred chunk collapses to 154 B - silently undoing this split while every test stays green. tests/unit/i18n/legalCatalog.test.ts fails loudly if that rule lands without excluding the legal fragments.
_size-limit-note-double-care: All-JS-combined raised 450 -> 470 kB for double-care detection and schedule drift (#423). Measured 2026-09-04 with this branch rebased onto main at f484634 (#428, the deferred legal catalog, on top of #420 Away Kit and #421 kiosk): main alone builds to 449.8 kB brotlied and this branch to 451.43 kB, so the feature costs +1.63 kB. Both readings were taken in one worktree from one npm ci, same node_modules, `npm run build && npm run size` on each side. THE RAISE IS NOT ALL THIS BRANCH: main now measures 449.8 kB against its own 450 kB limit - 200 B of headroom - so 450 no longer holds main plus any feature at all, and #428 (which freed ~10 kB by lazy-loading the legal catalog) has already been spent. Earlier notes on this branch proposing a raise off a 435/437 kB baseline predate #399, #412, #420, #421 and #428 and are stale in every number. No critical-path budget moved: Initial JS 17.15 kB (limit 62), Vendor 59.91 kB (limit 64), CSS 12.79 kB (limit 15), against 15.88 / 59.91 / 12.79 on main, and not one of those three limits is relaxed. The growth is the feature itself: the DoubleCarePrompt, DoubleCareCard and ScheduleDriftHint surfaces plus ~40 new i18n keys across en + es. Lazy-loading cannot move this number (`dist/assets/*.js` globs every emitted chunk), which is why the aggregate moves and the critical-path budgets do not. 470 kB is the smallest round step that holds this measurement with a real cushion (4.11%). MERGE ORDER: #419, #423, #424 and #425 each measure over 450 on this same main and each carry this same 470 kB, so no one of them depends on landing first - but their deltas are additive (+3.39, +1.63, +10.73, +5.49) and the all-four aggregate projects to ~471 kB, which 470 will NOT hold. Every one of them after the first must re-measure on the new main rather than assume 470 still stands.
